exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with your eyes on the horizon.
2. Gently draw your head straight back — as if making a double chin — without tilting up or down.
3. Hold for 3-5 seconds, feeling the deep front-neck muscles switch on.
4. Release slowly and repeat.
exercises.breathing: Exhale gently as you tuck; keep breathing steady throughout.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the motion small and pain-free; avoid forcing the head back with your hands.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid or reduce range if you feel dizziness, arm tingling or sharp pain.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Commonly used in physiotherapy programmes for forward-head posture and cervicogenic neck pain.

exercises.name: Deep Neck Flexor Activation
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back with a small towel under your head, knees bent.
2. Nod your head gently as if agreeing — a small, precise 'yes' motion.
3. Hold the nod for 5-10 seconds at a comfortable, low intensity.
4. Rest and repeat, keeping the superficial neck muscles relaxed.
exercises.breathing: Breathe slowly through the nose; do not hold your breath.
exercises.safety_notes: Activation should feel subtle (about 20-30% effort), never straining.
exercises.contraindications: Stop if you experience dizziness or headache increase.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Cornerstone of cervical motor-control retraining used by physiotherapists.

exercises.name: Suboccipital Release
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back and place a pair of tennis balls in a sock at the base of your skull.
2. Let your head rest heavily onto the balls, eyes soft.
3. Breathe deeply for 1-2 minutes, allowing the suboccipitals to soften.
4. Small, slow 'yes' nods add a gentle mobilisation.
exercises.breathing: Slow diaphragmatic breathing; exhale to release further.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep pressure moderate; never place balls on the top of the neck bones.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with acute neck injury, severe osteoporosis or if it provokes dizziness.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Frequently included in programmes for cervicogenic and tension-type headache.

exercises.name: Suboccipital Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall and interlace your fingers behind your head.
2. Allow your head to nod forward slightly, chin toward the ceiling-friendly tuck.
3. Let the weight of your arms apply a gentle traction at the skull base.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds, breathing easily.
exercises.breathing: Slow nasal breathing; soften on each exhale.
exercises.safety_notes: Traction should be gentle — the arms cradle, they do not pull hard.
exercises.contraindications: Discontinue with arm numbness, tingling or dizziness.

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit on one hand (same side as the stretch) to anchor the shoulder blade.
2. Rotate your head 45° away from the anchored side, looking toward the opposite armpit.
3. With the free hand, gently guide the head diagonally forward and down.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds on each side.
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you deepen gently; never bounce.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the guide hand's pressure light — under 10% of your strength.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid after acute whiplash or with radiating arm symptoms.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Scalene Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall and let one arm hang heavy to depress the shoulder.
2. Tilt your ear toward the opposite shoulder, keeping the face forward.
3. Rotate the head slightly upward and hold 20-30 seconds.
4. Repeat on the other side.
exercises.safety_notes: Do not pull hard; the scalenes protect nerves and vessels of the neck.
exercises.contraindications: Stop immediately if you feel tingling down the arm or lightheadedness.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Anchor one hand under the thigh or behind the back.
2. Tilt your head to the opposite side, ear to shoulder.
3. Optionally turn the chin slightly toward the collarbone.
4. Apply light overpressure with the free hand; hold 20-30 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep shoulders relaxed; avoid shrugging the stretching side.
exercises.contraindications: Use caution with any history of neck nerve symptoms.

exercises.name: Sternocleidomastoid Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall, looking forward.
2. Tilt your head back slightly and rotate it away from the side being stretched.
3. Feel the length along the front-side of the neck.
4. Hold 15-20 seconds and repeat on the other side.
exercises.breathing: Slow and even; avoid breath-holding with the head back.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep extension mild; the throat should never feel compressed.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with vertigo, cervical instability or vascular concerns.

exercises.name: Neck Rotation Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed.
2. Slowly turn your head to one side, chin over the shoulder.
3. Hold 3-5 seconds at a comfortable end range, then return to centre.
4. Repeat to the other side, keeping the motion smooth.
exercises.breathing: Exhale as you rotate; inhale returning to centre.
exercises.safety_notes: Rotate within comfort — no forcing or quick snapping motions.
exercises.contraindications: Reduce range with dizziness or if symptoms spread into the arm.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Cervical Extension Mobility
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall and slowly look up toward the ceiling.
2. Let the neck extend gently, mouth closed.
3. Pause 2-3 seconds, then return your gaze to eye level.
4. Repeat smoothly, one motion per 2-3 seconds.
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you look up; exhale returning.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the range comfortable; avoid if it provokes dizziness.
exercises.contraindications: Caution with spinal stenosis symptoms or balance issues.

exercises.name: Prone Cervical Extension Endurance
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down, forehead on a small folded towel.
2. Lift the head to align the neck with the spine — eyes to the floor.
3. Hold 5-10 seconds, keeping the shoulders heavy.
4. Lower with control and repeat.
exercises.breathing: Do not hold your breath; exhale during the lift.
exercises.safety_notes: Lift only to neutral alignment, not beyond.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with acute neck pain or extension-provoked symptoms.

exercises.name: Wall Posture Alignment
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with your heels, pelvis, upper back and head against a wall.
2. Perform a gentle chin tuck so the back of the head touches lightly.
3. Hold 20-30 seconds, breathing normally, feeling the tall stack.
4. Step away and try to keep the alignment for a minute.
exercises.safety_notes: If the head cannot comfortably reach the wall, keep the chin tuck alone.

exercises.name: Neck Side-Bend Mobility
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall, shoulders level.
2. Glide your ear toward one shoulder until the first comfortable stop.
3. Pause 2 seconds and return to centre.
4. Alternate sides in a slow rhythm.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep shoulders still — the motion comes from the neck only.
exercises.contraindications: Reduce range with nerve symptoms.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension Over Foam Roller
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind your mid back.
2. Support your head with your hands and extend over the roller.
3. Keep the ribs down — hinge at the thoracic spine, not the low back.
4. Move the roller an inch up the spine and repeat.
exercises.breathing: Inhale as you extend; exhale as you return.
exercises.safety_notes: Never roll the neck or low back; stop at the bottom of the shoulder blades.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with acute thoracic pain or known osteoporotic fracture risk.

exercises.name: TMJ Relaxed Jaw Position
exercises.instructions:
1. Rest the tongue gently on the roof of the mouth, lips closed, teeth apart.
2. Breathe through the nose, letting the jaw hang heavy.
3. Hold 1-2 minutes, noticing clenching habits melt away.
exercises.safety_notes: This is a relaxation exercise — there should be no effort.
exercises.clinical_relevance: First-line self-care habit for temporomandibular disorder (TMD) management.

exercises.name: Masseter Self-Massage
exercises.instructions:
1. Find the masseter by clenching once, then relaxing, over the cheek angle.
2. Use knuckles or fingertips to make slow circles on the tight band.
3. Add gentle sustained pressure on tender spots for 20-30 seconds.
4. Finish with slow, relaxed jaw opening.
exercises.breathing: Slow and easy; soften the jaw on each exhale.
exercises.safety_notes: Pressure should be comfortable, never sharp.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid over recently injured or surgically treated jaw areas.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: TMJ Controlled Opening
exercises.instructions:
1. Tongue on the palate, shoulders relaxed.
2. Open the mouth slowly and straight, as if yawning behind a mask.
3. Stop just before any click or deviation and close slowly.
4. Keep the motion mid-line, like a slow drawer.
exercises.safety_notes: Pain-free range only; never stretch into clicking.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Standard TMJ rehabilitation motor-control drill.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on the stretch side with the arm at 90°, elbow level with the shoulder.
2. Use the top hand to gently press the forearm toward the floor.
3. Keep the shoulder blade pinned forward by rolling slightly onto it.
4. Hold 30 seconds at a mild stretch.
exercises.breathing: Exhale to soften into the position.
exercises.safety_notes: Mild stretch only — this capsule tolerates low force.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with shoulder instability or after certain repair surgeries without guidance.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Used in overhead-thrower programmes addressing glenohumeral internal rotation deficit (GIRD).

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Bring one arm across your chest at shoulder height.
2. Hook the other forearm above the elbow and pull gently inward.
3. Keep the shoulder blade of the stretching arm from hiking up.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds each side.
exercises.breathing: Steady breathing, easing deeper on each exhale.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the elbow below shoulder height if the front of the shoulder pinches.

exercises.name: Doorway Pectoral Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Place your forearms on a door frame, elbows at shoulder height.
2. Step one foot forward into the doorway until a chest stretch appears.
3. Elbows lower bias the pec major; higher bias pec minor.
4. Hold 30 seconds, keeping ribs stacked over pelvis.
exercises.breathing: Inhale to lengthen the chest; exhale to settle deeper.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the stretch in the chest, not the shoulder front or low back.

exercises.name: Pendulum Exercise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lean on a table with the uninvolved arm, letting the other arm hang.
2. Relax the hanging arm completely and swing it in small circles.
3. Make 10 circles each direction, then gentle forward-back swings.
4. Let momentum, not muscle, do the work.
exercises.breathing: Relaxed; the arm must stay passive.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the torso still and the arm loose.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Early-stage shoulder rehabilitation for post-injury and post-surgical mobility.
exercises.dosage: 10 circles each direction, several times daily

exercises.name: Resistance Band External Rotation
exercises.instructions:
1. Hold a band with elbows bent 90° tucked at your sides; a rolled towel helps.
2. Keep elbows pinned and rotate both forearms outward against resistance.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades gently back as you rotate.
4. Return slowly over 3 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Use a light band — rotator cuffs respond to control, not load.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid pain at the top of motion; reduce resistance if form breaks.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Rotator-cuff strengthening staple for impingement-type shoulder programmes.

exercises.name: Scapular Clock
exercises.instructions:
1. Place a forearm on a wall at shoulder height.
2. Imagine a clock face on the wall and reach the shoulder blade toward 12, 3, 6 and 9.
3. Move slowly, isolating the shoulder blade from the arm.
4. Repeat both directions.
exercises.safety_notes: Small, controlled reaches; the arm stays still.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Internal Rotation
exercises.instructions:
1. Anchor a band at waist height beside you, elbow bent 90° at your side.
2. Rotate the forearm across your stomach against the resistance.
3. Keep the elbow glued to the ribs; move only at the shoulder.
4. Return slowly with control.
exercises.safety_notes: Light resistance; stop if the front of the shoulder pinches.

exercises.name: Scapular Retraction
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit or stand tall, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Draw the shoulder blades together and slightly down, as if pinching a pencil.
3. Hold 5 seconds without shrugging.
4. Release slowly and repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the neck long — no shrugging.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with back, head and wrists against a wall, elbows bent in a 'W'.
2. Slide the arms slowly up into a 'Y', keeping contact where possible.
3. Feel the shoulder blades rotating upward and outward.
4. Lower with the same control.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the low back flat — the goal is scapular motion, not lumbar arching.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down, arms overhead in a Y, thumbs toward the ceiling.
2. Lift the arms a few centimetres, initiating from the shoulder blades.
3. Hold 2-3 seconds at the top without craning the neck.
4. Lower slowly and repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Small range — this is a precision muscle, not a lifting drill.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prone T Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down, arms straight out to the sides, thumbs up.
2. Squeeze the shoulder blades to lift the arms into a T.
3. Hold 2-3 seconds, feeling the mid-back work.
4. Lower with control.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the neck relaxed, forehead down.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prone W Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down, elbows bent in a W beside the ribs.
2. Rotate the arms to lift the backs of the hands toward the ceiling.
3. Keep the elbows lightly touching the sides.
4. Pause 2 seconds and lower slowly.
exercises.safety_notes: Lift only as high as pain-free rotator control allows.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Serratus Anterior Punch
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, arms pointed at the ceiling.
2. Keeping the arms vertical, punch upward so the shoulder blades leave the floor.
3. Pause 2 seconds at the top, feeling the rib-side muscles.
4. Lower the shoulder blades slowly and repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Light or no weight to start; the motion is only a few centimetres.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Serratus activation drill for scapular dyskinesis programmes.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up Plus
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand arm's length from a wall, hands at chest height.
2. Perform a push-up, then at the top push extra — spreading the shoulder blades apart.
3. Hold the 'plus' position 2 seconds.
4. Return with control.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the body in one line; the plus should feel like the ribs pushing forward.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.instructions:
1. Hold a band at shoulder height, hands shoulder-width, palms down.
2. Pull the band apart to your chest, arms straight.
3. Squeeze the shoulder blades for 1-2 seconds.
4. Return slowly, keeping tension.
exercises.safety_notes: Choose a band that allows full range without shrugging.

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion Wand Exercise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back gripping a stick/broom wider than shoulders.
2. Use the healthy arm to help lift both arms overhead.
3. Guide to the highest comfortable point, elbows soft.
4. Lower with the good arm doing the braking.
exercises.safety_notes: Assisted range only — never push through pinching.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Standard post-operative and frozen-shoulder assisted ROM progression.

exercises.name: Towel Internal Rotation Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Drape a towel over the involved shoulder, holding the top end.
2. Reach behind your back with the other hand and grab the low end.
3. Pull the low end gently upward to stretch the back of the shoulder.
4. Hold 30 seconds at a mild intensity.
exercises.safety_notes: Mild stretch only; the posterior capsule is sensitive.
exercises.clinical_relevance: A common post-surgical stiffness exercise, often after rotator cuff repair.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.instructions:
1. Grip a stable bar or edge with an overhand grip.
2. Let the body hang with feet brushing the floor for safety.
3. Breathe deeply, letting the shoulders rise beside the ears.
4. Build from 10-second hangs.
exercises.breathing: Deep, relaxed breathing — the key to letting go.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep feet available for support; disengage if the elbow or shoulder pinches.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with shoulder instability symptoms or acute elbow complaints.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Eagle Arm Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Wrap one arm under the other, elbows crossing.
2. Press the palms together (or hold opposite shoulders).
3. Lift the elbows to shoulder height, sliding the top shoulder blade down.
4. Hold 30 seconds and unwind slowly.
exercises.safety_notes: Take the wrap only as far as comfort allows — shoulders vary widely.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prone on Elbows
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down and rise onto your forearms, elbows under shoulders.
2. Let the chest sink forward while the shoulder blades draw together.
3. Keep the neck long; breathe into the upper chest.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds, or rock gently side to side.
exercises.breathing: Slow deep breaths to open the front of the chest.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the low back comfortable — bias the upper back by squeezing the blades.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.instructions:
1. Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders.
2. Exhale: round the spine to the ceiling, tucking the tailbone (cat).
3. Inhale: tilt the pelvis, open the chest and let the belly sink (cow).
4. Flow slowly between the two for 10 breaths.
exercises.breathing: Movement follows breath — exhale cat, inhale cow.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the range comfortable for the wrists and low back.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.instructions:
1. From hands and knees, slide one arm under the chest, palm up.
2. Lower the shoulder and temple toward the floor.
3. Breathe into the twist for 30 seconds.
4. Optionally reach the top arm overhead to deepen.
exercises.safety_notes: Support the head with a cushion if the floor feels far.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Open Book Thoracic Rotation
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your side, knees stacked and hips at 90°, arms together at shoulder height.
2. Keeping knees glued, open the top arm like a book lid.
3. Follow the hand with the eyes until the shoulder blade nears the floor.
4. Breathe 3 deep breaths and close the book.
exercises.breathing: Inhale to open; exhale to soften deeper.
exercises.safety_notes: Block the knees with a pillow; the low back should not roll.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Extend one arm straight in front, palm down.
2. With the other hand, bend the wrist down so fingers point to the floor.
3. Keep the elbow straight and shoulder relaxed.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds at a mild stretch along the outer forearm.
exercises.safety_notes: Mild intensity — tendons respond poorly to aggressive stretching.
exercises.clinical_relevance: First-line flexibility exercise in lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) self-care.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Extend one arm straight, palm up.
2. With the other hand, bend the wrist back so fingers point to the ceiling.
3. Keep the elbow straight, stretching the inner forearm.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds gently.
exercises.safety_notes: Mild stretch only.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Used in medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow) management.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extension
exercises.instructions:
1. Rest the forearm on a table, hand over the edge, palm down, holding a light weight.
2. Use the other hand to lift the wrist to full extension.
3. Slowly lower the weight over 3-4 seconds using only the involved side.
4. Assist back up and repeat.
exercises.breathing: Exhale during the slow lowering phase.
exercises.safety_notes: Start with 0.5-1 kg; expect mild discomfort only, never sharp pain.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Heavily studied eccentric loading protocol for lateral elbow tendinopathy.
exercises.dosage: 3 x 15, daily or every other day

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Flexion
exercises.instructions:
1. Rest the forearm on a table, palm up, hand over the edge with a light weight.
2. Assist the wrist up into flexion with the free hand.
3. Lower slowly over 3-4 seconds under the involved side's control.
4. Assist up again; keep reps smooth.
exercises.safety_notes: Very light load to begin; stop with sharp inner-elbow pain.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Eccentric loading variant for medial elbow tendinopathy.

exercises.name: Wrist Pronation-Supination Mobility
exercises.instructions:
1. Bend the elbow to 90°, tucked at your side; hold a light stick upright.
2. Slowly rotate the forearm palm-down (pronation), like a doorknob.
3. Rotate palm-up (supination) through full comfortable range.
4. Alternate slowly for 10-15 cycles.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the upper arm still; motion is at the forearm only.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Radial Deviation Stretch (Thumb Side)
exercises.instructions:
1. Make a light fist with the thumb tucked inside the fingers.
2. Bend the wrist toward the pinky side (ulnar deviation).
3. Keep the arm straight in front, shoulder relaxed.
4. Hold 15-20 seconds at a gentle stretch along the thumb base.
exercises.safety_notes: Gentle intensity — this stretch can provoke de Quervain symptoms if forced.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Classic self-stretch in de Quervain's tenosynovitis programmes (Finkelstein-based).

exercises.name: Forearm Extensor Self-Massage
exercises.instructions:
1. Rest the forearm on a table, palm down, with a ball under the outer forearm.
2. Slowly roll along the muscle belly from elbow to mid-forearm.
3. Pause 20-30 seconds on tender spots, breathing slowly.
4. Flex and extend the fingers while paused to release deeper.
exercises.safety_notes: Avoid rolling directly on the bony elbow point or on swollen tissue.

exercises.name: Brachioradialis Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Extend the arm straight, palm down, thumb pointing down (pronated).
2. Grasp the thumb side of the hand and pull the wrist into flexion + ulnar deviation.
3. Keep the elbow fully straight.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: A very targeted stretch — keep it mild.

exercises.name: Supinator Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with the stick vertical, grasped palm-up (supinated).
2. Keeping the elbow straight, rotate the stick a half turn away from you.
3. The forearm moves into pronation, stretching the supinator.
4. Hold 20 seconds and repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Rotate only to comfortable pronation.

exercises.name: Median Nerve Glide
exercises.instructions:
1. Make a soft fist around your thumb, arm out to the side at shoulder height.
2. Bend the head away from the arm as you slowly straighten the elbow.
3. Feel a gentle 'slide' — never a stretch — through the arm.
4. Return before any tingling; glide 10-12 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Nerves need flossing, not stretching: stay below symptom threshold at all times.
exercises.contraindications: Do not push into numbness or tingling; stop if symptoms worsen afterwards.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Neural mobilisation used for median-nerve-sensitive presentations incl. carpal tunnel.

exercises.name: Ulnar Nerve Glide
exercises.instructions:
1. Make the 'OK' sign: thumb and index touching, other three fingers extended.
2. Bring the hand toward your ear, elbow bending out to the side, like holding a phone.
3. Slowly straighten the arm slightly and re-bend — a gentle seesaw.
4. Keep intensity minimal; glide 10 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Any inner-elbow tingling means back off — glide within comfort only.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid aggravating cubital tunnel symptoms.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Radial Nerve Glide
exercises.instructions:
1. Touch the back of your hand to your temple, thumb pointing down.
2. Slowly reach the hand diagonally up-and-out, elbow straightening.
3. Keep the motion smooth, like polishing a diagonal sky.
4. 10 easy glides, no tingling.
exercises.safety_notes: Glide, don't stretch; the radial nerve dislikes force.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.instructions:
1. Extend the arms, make soft fists.
2. Circle the wrists slowly, 10 each direction.
3. Keep the forearms still.
4. Reverse direction midway.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prayer Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Place palms together in front of the chest, elbows out.
2. Keeping palms touching, lower the hands until the wrists stretch.
3. Keep pressure equal on both palms.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep elbows high enough to feel the wrist, not elbow, stretch.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Tabletop Wrist Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Place hands flat on a table, fingers pointing back toward you.
2. Lean gently forward, keeping palms flat.
3. Stop at a comfortable stretch through the wrist crease and forearm.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Progress angle slowly; wrists adapt over weeks.
exercises.contraindications: Modify with a fist-on-table version if the flat-hand version provokes symptoms.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Isometric
exercises.instructions:
1. Rest the forearm on a table, palm down, wrist straight.
2. Press the back of the hand down into the other palm (or table edge).
3. Match force with the resistance — the wrist does not move.
4. Hold 10-30 seconds at a moderate, pain-free effort.
exercises.safety_notes: Isometrics should reduce, not raise, elbow pain; if pain increases, lower the force.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Isometric loading is an early-stage analgesic protocol for tendinopathy.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Finger Spread
exercises.instructions:
1. Place the hand flat on a table, palm down.
2. Spread the fingers apart as far as comfortable.
3. Hold 3-5 seconds, then bring them back together.
4. Repeat rhythmically.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Fist to Fan
exercises.instructions:
1. Open the hand wide, fingers spread.
2. Slowly curl into a full, tight fist, thumb outside.
3. Squeeze 2 seconds, then explode gently open into the fan.
4. Repeat 10-15 times.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Finger Tendon Gliding Exercise
exercises.instructions:
1. Start with fingers straight (straight position).
2. Bend only the big knuckles — 'table top'.
3. Then hook the fingers — 'hook fist'.
4. Then full fist, then straight fist; flow 5-10 cycles.
exercises.safety_notes: Move through comfortable ranges; no forcing swollen or injured joints.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Standard flexor-tendon and carpal-tunnel rehabilitation gliding sequence.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Thumb Stretch Series
exercises.instructions:
1. Gently pull the thumb back and away from the palm (extension/abduction).
2. Hold 10-15 seconds.
3. Then tuck the thumb across the palm under the fingers for 10-15 seconds.
4. Repeat the series 3 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Very gentle — thumb joints are small.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Used in first-carpometacarpal (basal thumb) osteoarthritis programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Thenar Self-Massage
exercises.instructions:
1. Use the opposite thumb to make slow circles on the fleshy thumb pad.
2. Work from the wrist to the thumb joint.
3. Pause 20 seconds on tender knots.
4. Finish by moving the thumb through its circle (opposition).
exercises.safety_notes: Avoid pressing on numb or tingling areas.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Towel Squeeze
exercises.instructions:
1. Roll a small towel and hold it in one hand.
2. Squeeze firmly for 3-5 seconds.
3. Release partially and repeat.
4. Keep the wrist neutral throughout.
exercises.safety_notes: Avoid maximal gripping with acute tendon irritation.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Marble Pickup
exercises.instructions:
1. Place 10-20 marbles (or beans) on one side of a bowl.
2. Pick them up one at a time with a pincer or full-grip and move them across.
3. Work with focus on controlled finger motion.
4. Reverse hands and repeat.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Finger Extension With Rubber Band
exercises.instructions:
1. Loop a light rubber band around all five fingertips.
2. Spread the fingers open against the band's resistance.
3. Hold 2 seconds, return slowly.
4. Keep the band light — this is endurance, not max force.
exercises.safety_notes: Point bands away from the face.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel and sit the hips back onto the heels.
2. Walk the hands forward, resting the forehead down.
3. Let the back round softly; breathe into the ribs.
4. Hold 30-60 seconds, walking hands to bias each side.
exercises.safety_notes: Pad behind the knees or widen them if hips or knees complain.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Supine Spinal Twist
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, arms out in a T.
2. Draw the knees halfway up and let them fall gently to one side.
3. Turn the head opposite the knees; shoulders stay heavy.
4. Breathe 30-45 seconds and switch sides.
exercises.breathing: Long exhales deepen the twist safely.
exercises.safety_notes: Place a cushion under the knees to reduce twist depth.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Single Knee-to-Chest
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, legs straight.
2. Draw one knee toward the chest with both hands.
3. Keep the other leg heavy on the floor.
4. Hold 30 seconds; repeat 2-3 times per leg.
exercises.breathing: Exhale to draw the knee closer.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the tailbone on the floor; avoid lifting the head.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing QL Side-Bend Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand tall, feet hip-width; reach one arm overhead.
2. Bend directly sideways, reaching long over the head.
3. Push the opposite hip gently toward the floor.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds, breathing into the stretched side.
exercises.breathing: Direct slow breaths into the ribs on the open side.
exercises.safety_notes: Bend like a willow, not an arch — keep the body in one plane.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie face down, hands under the shoulders.
2. Press the chest up, keeping the hips on the floor.
3. Rise only as far as comfortable; exhale at the top.
4. Lower slowly; repeat 10 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the low back relaxed — arms do the pressing. Stop if symptoms travel down a leg.
exercises.contraindications: Avoid with suspected acute disc issues that worsen with extension or leg symptoms.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Extension-based exercise common in mechanical low-back care (McKenzie method family).

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
2. Flatten the low back into the floor by tilting the pelvis back.
3. Feel the deep abdominals engage gently.
4. Hold 5 seconds, release halfway; repeat 10-15 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Subtle motion of a few degrees — no forcing.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Foundational motor-control drill in low-back pain rehabilitation.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, arms vertical, knees stacked over hips at 90°.
2. Press the low back gently into the floor.
3. Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly toward the floor.
4. Return and alternate; the back never arches.
exercises.safety_notes: If the back arches, shorten the lever — move legs only.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.instructions:
1. From hands and knees, find a neutral spine.
2. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
3. Imagine balancing a wine glass on your low back.
4. Hold 3-5 seconds; switch sides with control.
exercises.safety_notes: Move limbs without letting the pelvis tilt or rotate.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Core-stabilisation staple for low-back rehabilitation programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet hip-width.
2. Drive through the heels to lift the hips into a straight line.
3. Squeeze the glutes at the top for 2 seconds — ribs stay down.
4. Lower one vertebra at a time.
exercises.safety_notes: If hamstrings cramp, feet closer to hips; glutes lead, not low back.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie comfortably, one hand on the chest, one on the belly.
2. Inhale through the nose so the belly hand rises first.
3. Exhale slowly through pursed lips, belly falling.
4. Continue 3-5 minutes at an easy rhythm (about 6 breaths/minute).
exercises.clinical_relevance: Foundation of relaxation, COPD and chronic pain breathing retraining programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Box Breathing
exercises.instructions:
1. Inhale through the nose for 4 counts.
2. Hold gently for 4 counts.
3. Exhale smoothly for 4 counts.
4. Hold empty for 4; repeat the square 8-10 rounds.
exercises.safety_notes: If light-headed, drop the holds; keep counts shorter.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with one leg extended, the other bent with foot to inner thigh.
2. Hinge forward from the hips, chest leading.
3. Rest hands on the floor, a chair seat, or the shin.
4. Hold 30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: A flat-back fold halfway down beats a rounded reach to the toes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Pelvic Floor Activation
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie with knees bent; breathe normally.
2. Gently draw the pelvic floor up and in, as if stopping the flow of urine.
3. Hold 3-5 seconds at 30-50% effort, fully releasing between.
4. Coordinate with an exhale; repeat 10 times.
exercises.safety_notes: Full relaxation between contractions matters as much as the lift.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Core component of pelvic-health physiotherapy programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Seated Trunk Rotation
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall on a chair, feet flat.
2. Hold the seat back with both hands on one side.
3. Rotate the chest around a tall spine, sitting bones even.
4. Hold 20 seconds; repeat twice per side.
exercises.breathing: Inhale to lengthen; exhale to rotate further.
exercises.safety_notes: Rotate the ribcage, not just the shoulders or neck.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Seated Cat-Cow
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with hands on knees, feet flat.
2. Exhale: round back, tuck chin and tailbone.
3. Inhale: lift chest and tailbone, gaze slightly up.
4. Flow 10 slow cycles.
exercises.breathing: Exhale to round, inhale to arch.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Seated Figure-4 Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall and cross one ankle over the opposite knee, making a figure 4.
2. Keep the crossed knee open (falling outward).
3. Hinge forward from the hips with a tall spine until a stretch appears in the buttock.
4. Hold 30 seconds; switch sides.
exercises.safety_notes: Stretch the buttock, not the knee: never press down on the crossed knee.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Piriformis and deep rotator stretch common in sciatica-adjacent programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
exercises.instructions:
1. From all fours, bring one knee forward and lay it diagonally under the chest.
2. Slide the other leg long behind, toes untucked.
3. Level the hips (a pillow under the buttock helps) and settle.
4. Stay upright or fold forward onto the forearms for 30-60 seconds.
exercises.breathing: Slow breathing releases the hip on every exhale.
exercises.safety_notes: Knee discomfort means back off: do the figure-4 version instead.
exercises.contraindications: Careful with known hip impingement or knee injuries.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel on one knee (cushion under it), the other foot forward.
2. Tuck the tailbone to posteriorly tilt the pelvis — this is the stretch.
3. Squeeze the back-leg glute and gently shift forward a few centimetres.
4. Hold 30 seconds, ribs stacked over the pelvis.
exercises.breathing: Exhale to tuck; breathe into the front of the hip.
exercises.safety_notes: The pelvis tuck comes first; without it the low back takes the stretch.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Key exercise for shortened hip flexors in sedentary and postpartum populations.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
aliases: deep hip flexor and quad stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Face away from a wall/couch, back knee on a cushion, shin up the wall.
2. Squeeze the back glute to tuck the pelvis before anything else.
3. Bring the torso upright in stages — hands to floor, then tall.
4. Breathe 45+ seconds; intensity should be strong but tolerable.
exercises.breathing: Slow, deliberate breathing; do not brace.
exercises.safety_notes: Progress slowly over weeks; knee pain means raise the foot higher or reduce knee bend.
exercises.contraindications: Skip with anterior knee pain or recent patellar injury.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Butterfly Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the soles of the feet together, knees out.
2. Hold the ankles, sit tall.
3. Hinge forward from the hips, leading with the chest.
4. Hold 30-60 seconds; knees float — no pressing.
exercises.breathing: Long exhales; imagine the knees floating up on inhales.
exercises.safety_notes: Never bounce or push knees down; gravity and time do the work.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the front leg bent 90° in front and the back leg bent 90° to the side.
2. Sit tall, hands lightly behind for balance.
3. Lead the chest over the front shin for external-rotation bias.
4. Switch legs by rotating the knees together through the middle.
exercises.breathing: Exhale into each position; 30-45 seconds each side.
exercises.safety_notes: Pad under the back knee; keep the sit bones heavy.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Take a long step back with one leg, both feet pointing forward.
2. Tuck the tailbone, squeeze the back glute.
3. Shift forward until the front of the back hip lengthens.
4. Hold 30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the back knee soft; ribs down.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Glute Bridge March
exercises.instructions:
1. Lift into a glute bridge and hold the line.
2. Lift one knee a few centimetres toward the chest without dropping a hip.
3. Place it down and lift the other — marching.
4. Keep the hips level like headlights.
exercises.safety_notes: If hips wobble, lower and re-bridge; quality first.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your side, body straight, slight forward lean.
2. Lift the top leg 30-45°, heel slightly behind the line of the body.
3. Toes point forward — lead with the heel.
4. Lower slowly; feel the side-of-hip muscle work.
exercises.safety_notes: Small range with control beats big kicks with momentum.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Gluteus medius strengthening for hip and knee rehabilitation, pelvic drop (Trendelenburg).

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your side, knees bent ~45°, heels together, hips stacked.
2. Keeping the feet touching, rotate the top knee open like a clam.
3. Feel the glute behind the hip bone — not the front.
4. Close slowly; repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: If you feel it at the front of the hip, roll the toes slightly down.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Classic gluteal activation drill; often early in hip/knee rehab programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing Hip Drop (Wall Support)
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand side-on to a wall, one hand on it, feet together.
2. Keep both knees straight and drop the inner hip toward the floor.
3. Then hitch it up above level, shortening the waist.
4. Move smoothly through drops and hitches.
exercises.safety_notes: Small motion; the standing hip does the work.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand on one leg with light support at a wall.
2. Swing the free leg in slow, large circles.
3. 8 circles each direction, keeping the torso still.
4. Switch legs.
exercises.safety_notes: Circles grow gradually; support as needed for balance.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Leg Swings
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand side-on to a wall, one hand on it.
2. Swing the inside leg forward and back like a pendulum.
3. Start small, grow the arc gradually — 15-20 swings.
4. Turn around and swing the other leg.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the swing relaxed; no forcing at the end range.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: ITB Foam Roll
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie side-on with the roller under the outer thigh, other leg in front for support.
2. Roll slowly from just below the hip to just above the knee.
3. Pause 20-30 seconds on tender spots.
4. Keep the discomfort at 'uncomfortable but bearable' — never sharp.
exercises.safety_notes: Never roll over bony prominences; the ITB itself cannot be 'stretched' — work the attached muscles.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Self-myofascial release used around ITB friction syndrome and runner's knee care.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Take a wide stance, toes slightly out.
2. Shift the hips sideways, bending one knee over its foot.
3. Feel the inner thigh of the straight leg lengthen.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds each side.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the bent knee tracking over the middle toes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Sciatic Nerve Glide (Supine)
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back with a strap around one foot.
2. Straighten the knee to a comfortable tension, then flex the ankle (nerve tension).
3. Bend the knee again while keeping the leg up (nerve slack) — alternate like flossing.
4. 10-12 cycles, always below symptom threshold.
exercises.safety_notes: Never stretch into tingling or shooting sensations — glide lightly.
exercises.contraindications: Not for acute severe nerve pain; consult a clinician first.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Neural mobilisation for sciatic-nerve-sensitive presentations.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation Mobility
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit tall; bring one ankle to rest just above the opposite knee.
2. Hold the knee and shin, and gently rotate the hip inward by drawing the knee toward the midline.
3. Keep the sit bones even; move with breath.
4. 10 slow rotations per hip.
exercises.safety_notes: Small arc, no knee pressure.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
2. Descend into the deepest comfortable squat, heels down.
3. Use elbows to gently press knees out; chest tall.
4. Hold 20-60 seconds, rocking gently side to side.
exercises.breathing: Slow, easy breathing in the bottom.
exercises.safety_notes: Heels lift? Support them on a book; knees track over toes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Side-Lying SI Joint Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your side at the edge of a bed, top knee dropped over the edge in front.
2. Let the top shoulder rotate back toward the ceiling.
3. Breathe into the back of the pelvis for 30 seconds.
4. Repeat on the other side.
exercises.safety_notes: Support the dropped knee with a cushion.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand on one leg (wall for balance), holding the other ankle behind you.
2. Keep knees together and tuck the tailbone.
3. Draw the knee slightly back only if the front hip needs more.
4. Hold 30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: No twisting at the knee; if it tweaks the knee, use the side-lying version.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your side, bottom arm supporting the head.
2. Bend the top knee and hold the ankle behind you.
3. Keep the thigh in line with the body; tailbone tucked.
4. Hold 30 seconds and rotate legs.
exercises.safety_notes: Knee-friendly alternative when standing version pinches.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch With Strap
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back and loop a strap under one foot.
2. Raise the leg, knee nearly straight, to a clear hamstring stretch.
3. Keep the other leg heavy on the floor.
4. Hold 30 seconds; the knee can stay softly bent.
exercises.breathing: Exhale to invite the leg higher.
exercises.safety_notes: Stretch the back of the thigh, not behind the knee — never yank.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Short-Arc Quadriceps Exercise
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back with a rolled towel (~15 cm) under one knee.
2. Straighten that knee, sliding the foot along the floor and lifting the heel.
3. Squeeze the thigh hard at the top for 3 seconds.
4. Lower slowly; repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the low back relaxed; only the knee works.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Early quadriceps re-education after knee surgery/injury; targets VMO recruitment.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit long, one knee bent; straighten the other leg, quad squeezed.
2. Lift the straight leg to the height of the bent knee.
3. Hold 2-3 seconds; lower with control.
4. Keep the pelvis still.
exercises.safety_notes: If the hip front grips, reduce height; quality over height.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Foundational quadriceps/hip-flexor exercise post knee surgery.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Terminal Knee Extension (Band)
exercises.instructions:
1. Loop a band behind the knee, anchored at knee height.
2. Start with the exercised knee slightly bent, weight on that leg.
3. Straighten the knee fully against the band, squeezing the quad.
4. Return slowly to the slight bend; repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Light band; motion is the last 20-30° of extension.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Terminal extension drills for lockout strength and VMO function in knee rehab.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with your back to a wall, feet two shoe-lengths out.
2. Slide down until knees are bent ~45-60°, knees over ankles.
3. Hold, breathing steadily, back flat on the wall.
4. Build from 20 to 60 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep thighs parallel; stop if pain under the kneecap is sharp.

exercises.name: Heel Slides
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, legs long.
2. Slowly slide one heel toward the buttocks, bending the knee.
3. Pause at the end of comfortable flexion for 3 seconds.
4. Slide back out; use a strap around the foot for assistance.
exercises.safety_notes: Smooth, pain-free arcs; use the strap rather than forcing.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Early knee-flexion ROM exercise after knee surgery or injury.

exercises.name: Patellar Mobilization
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the knee straight and completely relaxed (foot supported).
2. Grip the kneecap edges and glide it gently up, down, inward and outward.
3. Hold each direction 5-10 seconds.
4. Keep the quad floppy — tension blocks the glide.
exercises.safety_notes: The kneecap should move only millimetres; never force.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Used post knee surgery and in patellofemoral stiffness programmes.

exercises.name: Popliteus Stretch (Soleus Bias)
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand in a short lunge, hands on a wall, back knee slightly bent.
2. Keep the back heel down and rotate the back foot slightly inward.
3. Gently shift the back knee forward and across the midline.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds for a deep, behind-the-knee stretch.
exercises.safety_notes: A stretch behind the knee should feel broad, never sharp or circular.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing ITB Cross-Over Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Cross the leg to be stretched behind the other.
2. Side-bend the torso away, pushing the hip out.
3. Feel the band tighten along the outer hip to the knee.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the stretch along the outer thigh, not the low back.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Gastrocnemius Wall Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Face a wall in a staggered stance, hands on the wall.
2. Keep the back leg straight, heel pressed down, toes forward.
3. Shift forward until the calf stretches clearly.
4. Hold 30 seconds per leg.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the back heel grounded; heel lifting reduces the stretch.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Soleus Wall Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand close to a wall, one foot back — this time with the back knee bent.
2. Keep the heel down and shift the back knee toward the wall.
3. The lower calf / Achilles area should stretch, not the upper calf.
4. Hold 30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: Bending the knee is the point — it isolates soleus over gastrocnemius.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Soleus length matters in Achilles tendinopathy and running-injury programmes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Downward Dog Pedaling
exercises.instructions:
1. From hands and knees, lift the hips into an inverted V.
2. Bend one knee, sending the opposite heel toward the floor.
3. Pedal the heels slowly, alternating for 20-30 seconds.
4. Finish with both heels reaching down.
exercises.breathing: Even breathing; keep the neck long.
exercises.safety_notes: Bend the knees generously if the low back rounds.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Eccentric Heel Drop (Alfredson)
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand on a step with the balls of the feet, heels hanging off.
2. Rise onto both tiptoes (use the healthy leg to help).
3. Shift weight to the involved leg and lower the heel below the step over 3-4 seconds.
4. Use the good leg to rise again; repeat.
exercises.safety_notes: Expect mild tendon discomfort; sharp pain means reduce range or load.
exercises.clinical_relevance: The Alfredson eccentric protocol — landmark rehabilitation programme for mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy.
exercises.dosage: 3 x 15, twice daily (straight and bent knee)

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand with the balls of the feet on flat ground, hand on a wall for balance.
2. Rise as high as possible onto the toes — a full heel lift.
3. Pause 1-2 seconds at the top.
4. Lower slowly over 3 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Do them with a slight knee bend to bias soleus as a variation.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Tibialis Anterior Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel with the tops of the feet on the floor (cushion under the ankles).
2. Sit the hips gently back toward the heels, toes pointing back.
3. Feel the front-of-shin muscles lengthen.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds; use hands on the floor to control weight.
exercises.safety_notes: Pad the ankles; come up if the knees or ankles complain.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Peroneal Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with one leg crossed over the other knee.
2. Hold the foot and gently draw it into inversion — sole turning inward/up.
3. Add slight plantarflexion to deepen the outer-leg stretch.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds per side.
exercises.safety_notes: Gentle — the peroneals cross a mobile joint.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Calf Foam Roll
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit on the floor with the calf on a roller, hands behind for support.
2. Roll slowly from ankle to the back of the knee.
3. Rotate the leg in and out to reach the inner and outer calf.
4. Pause 20-30 seconds on tender spots; circle the ankle while paused.
exercises.safety_notes: Avoid the back of the knee pit itself.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the foot lifted slightly off the floor.
2. Circle the ankle slowly — 10 each direction.
3. Make the circles as large as the joint allows.
4. Point and flex the foot between sets.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with one foot lifted.
2. Trace each letter of the alphabet in the air with the big toe.
3. Move slowly and make large letters.
4. Repeat with the other foot.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Common early-home-rehab mobility drill after ankle sprain.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobility
exercises.instructions:
1. Place the toes of one foot a hand-width from a wall.
2. Keep the heel down and drive the knee straight toward the wall.
3. If the knee touches easily, move the foot back a centimetre and repeat.
4. Find the edge of range; 10-15 pumps per ankle.
exercises.safety_notes: The heel must stay glued down — that's the measurement and the stretch.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Dorsiflexion deficit after ankle sprain is a re-injury risk factor; this is the standard self-mobilisation.

exercises.name: Ankle Inversion Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the ankle resting on the opposite knee.
2. Cup the heel and turn the sole of the foot upward and inward.
3. Move into the comfortable end range, hold 5 seconds, release.
4. Repeat 10 times per ankle.
exercises.safety_notes: Post-sprain stiffness improves slowly; never force past pinching.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Eversion
exercises.instructions:
1. Loop a band around the mid-foot and anchor it to the inside leg of a table (or hold it).
2. Keep the leg still and rotate the sole of the foot outward against the band.
3. Pause 1 second, return slowly.
4. Keep the motion at the ankle — the knee doesn't move.
exercises.safety_notes: Light band; high reps build tendon tolerance.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Peroneal strengthening is central to lateral ankle sprain rehabilitation.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Inversion
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the band around the mid-foot, anchored to the outside.
2. Draw the sole of the foot inward and up against the band.
3. Keep the ankle at ~90°; the heel may lift slightly.
4. Return with control.
exercises.safety_notes: Light resistance; smooth tempo.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Tibialis posterior strengthening for posterior tibial tendon dysfunction and flat-foot care.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
exercises.instructions:
1. Anchor a band around the top of the foot, held in front.
2. Pull the toes and foot up toward the shin against resistance.
3. Keep the heel planted; only the ankle moves.
4. Lower slowly.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand near a wall for safety and lift one foot.
2. Balance on the other leg with a soft, tall posture.
3. Aim for 30 seconds; harder = eyes closed or uneven surface.
4. Repeat 3 times per leg.
exercises.safety_notes: Fingertip support first; progress by removing it.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Proprioceptive training reduces recurrent ankle sprain risk.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance (Eyes Closed)
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand on one leg near a wall, then close the eyes.
2. Feel the foot and ankle making rapid small corrections.
3. Balance up to 30 seconds; open eyes if you tip.
4. Repeat 3 times per leg.
exercises.safety_notes: Always within arm's reach of a wall.

exercises.name: Plantar Fascia Ball Massage
exercises.instructions:
1. Place a ball (tennis/golf) under the arch of the foot while seated.
2. Roll slowly from heel to the ball of the foot.
3. Pause 15-20 seconds on tender spots; flex the toes there.
4. Spend 1-2 minutes per foot.
exercises.safety_notes: Seated pressure first; standing adds much more intensity.
exercises.clinical_relevance: First-line self-care for plantar fascia pain, especially before first steps in the morning.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Plantar Fascia Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the affected foot crossed over the knee.
2. Pull the toes back toward the shin until the arch tightens like a string.
3. With the other thumb, massage the taut arch gently.
4. Hold 10 seconds x 10 reps — best done before standing in the morning.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Strongly evidence-supported self-stretch for plantar heel pain.

exercises.name: Toe Towel Scrunch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with a flat towel on the floor under one foot.
2. Keeping the heel planted, scrunch the towel toward you with the toes.
3. Gather, release, and repeat until the towel is bunched.
4. Smooth it out and repeat; change feet.
exercises.safety_notes: Cramping is common at first — rest and continue.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Intrinsic foot muscle strengthening for arch support and plantar fascia programmes.

exercises.name: Toe Yoga
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand or sit with feet flat, weight even.
2. Lift only the big toes, keeping the other four down.
3. Then press the big toes down and lift the four lesser toes.
4. Alternate slowly 10-15 times, feet flat throughout.
exercises.safety_notes: It's fine if coordination is clumsy at first — that's the point.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Dissociated toe control trains intrinsic foot muscles for arch control.

exercises.name: Short Foot Exercise
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand barefoot with the foot flat, toes relaxed and straight.
2. Without curling the toes, draw the ball of the big toe toward the heel.
3. The arch domes up; the foot 'shortens'.
4. Hold 5-8 seconds; keep the ankle neutral.
exercises.safety_notes: If the toes curl or the ankle rolls out, restart smaller.
exercises.clinical_relevance: Evidence-supported intrinsic foot muscle exercise, used for flat foot and plantar fascia programmes.

exercises.name: Big Toe Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel in a lunge with the big toe of the back foot tucked under.
2. Gently sit the hips toward the heel, extending the big toe.
3. Keep the other four toes relaxed on the floor.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds; the base of the big toe should stretch.
exercises.safety_notes: Progress over weeks; the joint adapts gradually.
exercises.clinical_relevance: First MTP extension matters for walking mechanics and hallux rigidus care.

exercises.name: Seated Toe Spreader Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with the foot on the opposite knee.
2. Interlace the fingers of the opposite hand between the toes.
3. Gently rotate and spread for 20-30 seconds.
4. Repeat once more per foot.
exercises.safety_notes: Be extra gentle with the little toes.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Intrinsic-Offloaded Heel Raise
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand near a wall with the big toes pressed gently into the floor.
2. Keeping that pressure, rise to the heels' tops.
3. The arch stays domed and the toes stay long — no clawing.
4. Lower over 3 seconds.
exercises.safety_notes: Quality of arch doming is the goal; lower the height if toes claw.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Toe Extensor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel with the tops of the toes tucked under (cushion under the ankles).
2. Sit the hips back slightly, pointing the toes down.
3. The tops of the feet and toes stretch.
4. Hold 20-30 seconds gently.
exercises.safety_notes: Mild intensity; the small toe joints adapt slowly.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Kneeling Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Kneel on one knee with the front foot flat.
2. Shift the front knee far forward over or past the toes, heel down.
3. Pause at the deepest comfortable angle for 3-5 seconds.
4. Return and repeat 10 times per ankle.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep the foot flat and the arch from collapsing inward.

media.credit: AI-generated illustration created for the Easeur Exercise Knowledge Base (no third-party rights)

exercises.name: Tibialis Posterior Self-Release
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit with a ball tucked behind the inner shin bone, above the ankle.
2. Press the calf into the ball and slide slowly up the inner calf.
3. Pause on tender spots for 20-30 seconds; circle the foot while paused.
4. Work the inner calf in 3-4 lines.
exercises.safety_notes: Stay on muscle, off the sharp shin bone edge.

exercises.name: Towel-Marble Combo Pickup
exercises.instructions:
1. Place marbles on the floor before a chair, a cup beside them.
2. Using only the toes of one foot, pick up marbles into the cup.
3. Ten marbles per foot; alternate feet.
4. Progress by doing it standing on one leg.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand tall, arms out to the sides.
2. Draw small circles forward, growing larger over 10 reps.
3. Reverse direction for 10 more.
4. Keep the neck relaxed and ribs stacked.

exercises.name: Standing Large Hip Circles
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand on one leg, hands on a wall or rail.
2. Swing the free leg in the biggest relaxed circle possible.
3. 10 clockwise, 10 counter-clockwise.
4. Switch legs; stay tall and easy.
exercises.safety_notes: Circles grow with warmth; never force cold hips.

exercises.name: Walking Hamstring Reach
exercises.instructions:
1. Walk two steps, then kick one leg straight ahead with the heel down.
2. Hinge the torso over the straight leg with a flat back.
3. Feel a brief hamstring stretch (2 seconds), stand tall.
4. Continue alternating for 10 reaches per leg.
exercises.safety_notes: Dynamic, not ballistic — smooth reach, no bouncing.

exercises.name: Lateral Leg Swings
exercises.instructions:
1. Face a wall, both hands on it, weight on one leg.
2. Swing the free leg across the body and out to the side.
3. Keep the torso tall and the swing relaxed.
4. 15 swings, then switch legs.
exercises.safety_notes: Start small and grow the arc.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Step into a long lunge, both hands inside the front foot.
2. Drop the back knee if needed; the front ankle stays deep.
3. Place one forearm down and rotate the other arm to the ceiling.
4. Hold 3 breaths; switch the rotation, then switch legs.
exercises.breathing: Inhale to rotate open; exhale to soften.
exercises.safety_notes: Elevate hands on a block if the floor is far.

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
exercises.instructions:
1. Sit sideways against a wall and swing the legs up as you lie back.
2. Rest the heels on the wall, arms open, palms up.
3. Close the eyes and breathe slowly for 5-10 minutes.
4. Bend the knees and roll to the side to exit.
exercises.safety_notes: Keep a slight knee bend or move the hips away from the wall if hamstrings grip.

exercises.name: Supine Relaxation (Savasana)
exercises.instructions:
1. Lie on your back, limbs comfortable and symmetrical, palms up.
2. Systematically relax: feet, calves, thighs, hips, belly, chest, arms, neck, face.
3. Let the breath be quiet and unforced.
4. Rest 5-15 minutes, staying awake but deeply calm.

exercises.name: Gentle Cool-Down Walk
exercises.instructions:
1. After hard exercise, drop to an easy conversational pace.
2. Walk 5-10 minutes, letting the breath settle.
3. Add long exhales: in through the nose, slowly out.
4. Finish with a full-body stretch of the day's tightest areas.

exercises.name: Body Scan Stretch Flow
exercises.instructions:
1. From standing, roll down slowly and hang (knees soft).
2. Add gentle side reaches, then a lunge with a rotation.
3. Drop to a deep squat hold, then sit into a hamstring stretch each side.
4. Roll back up, finishing with 3 slow breaths standing tall.
exercises.breathing: Move on the exhale; one breath per position.
exercises.safety_notes: Modify any position; the flow is a menu, not a test.

exercises.name: Standing Side Body Stretch
exercises.instructions:
1. Stand tall, interlace the fingers and reach overhead.
2. Arc gently to one side, hips even.
3. Breathe into the lengthening side for 20-30 seconds.
4. Return through centre and arc to the other side.
exercises.breathing: Direct breath into the open ribs.
